title: requirement_matching_result.json -- payout requirement matches per coverage v0.2
description: Produced by claim-analysis's checkpoint 4 (Requirement Matching). Grouped per coverage, joining on coverage_result.json's coverage_name/standardized_coverage_name. v0.2: carries upstream_policy_snapshot -- the policy-layer digest set this result was derived from. Optional in the schema because an artifact that references no policy clause has nothing to bind to; the DAO makes it mandatory the moment a clause reference exists, and refuses a stale one.

upstream_policy_snapshot.description: The policy-layer snapshot this artifact was derived from (Part 11I). Required whenever the artifact carries at least one policy reference: a downstream result is an assertion about what the policy layer said when it was written, so it records which bytes it read. The DAO recomputes this at write time and refuses a mismatch; `dao.py policy-snapshot` prints the current value. Per-document digests cover the normalized contract, boundary inventory, reference tables, processed source text, manifest entry (page_map included) and governing parent coverage -- the same set the document's audit binds to.

requirement_text.description: The payout condition being checked, from the matched policy clause.

clause_ref.description: The policy condition this requirement is drawn from, addressed in one of two ways. UID form ({document_id, clause_uid, condition_uid, display_clause_id?}) points into policy-pipeline's normalized_policy_clause_{document_id}.json; both UIDs are recomputed from source, so it is the stronger address and it addresses one CONDITION inside a clause, which is the granularity requirement matching wants. It requires the document to have been normalized. SOURCE form ({document_id, page, quote, display_clause_id?}) addresses the condition by its verbatim location in the processed text, for a text_only_no_normalization document (normalization is opt-in, so most policy documents have no clause contract). The source form is honestly coarser -- a page+quote names the text a requirement rests on, not a pre-parsed condition item -- so quote the specific condition sentence, not the whole clause. The DAO verifies it as strictly: the page must exist and the quote must appear verbatim on it. null means the requirement could not be tied to a specific clause at all, and must NOT be used for a condition that was found but seemed unaddressable.

allOf.description: A UID-form reference names one CONDITION, so clause_uid without condition_uid is incomplete rather than a source-form reference. Stated separately from the oneOf below so the error names the missing field instead of only reporting that no branch matched.

status.description: uncertain covers missing/ambiguous evidence -- pair with review_required:true.

evidence_references.description: May be empty only when status is uncertain due to genuinely absent evidence.

allOf.description: Rule: met/not_met requirements must cite at least one piece of evidence.
